source_reading: All 247 complete source units were read in three consecutive physical-order batches before target curation; root was notified immediately after source reading. All final retained source-target-rationale triples were then reread in three batches. Every rationale subsequently revised during author or peer checking was reread with its complete source and target.

source_units.text: Son, do not envy evil men, and do not desire to be with them;
for their heart meditates lies, and their lips speak toils.
With wisdom a house is built, and with understanding it is raised upright;
with discernment store-rooms are filled from every precious and good wealth.
A wise person is better than a strong one, and a man with understanding than a great cultivated estate;
with steering war takes place, and help is with a deliberative heart.
Wisdom and good reflection are in the gates of the wise; the wise do not turn from the mouth of the Lord,
but deliberate in councils. Death meets the uneducated,
and a fool dies in sins; and impurity will be defiled in a pestilent man,
on an evil day and on a day of affliction, until he fails.
Rescue those being led to death, and ransom those being killed; do not hold back.
But if you say, “I do not know this person,” know that the Lord knows everyone’s hearts, and the One who fashioned breath for all Himself knows everything, and repays each one according to his works.
Eat honey, son, for a honeycomb is good, so that your throat may be sweetened;
in this way you will perceive wisdom for your own life; for if you find it, your end will be good, and hope will not abandon you.
Do not bring an impious person to the pasture of the righteous, and do not be deceived by a filled belly;
for the righteous will fall seven times and rise, but the impious will grow weak amid evils.
If your enemy falls, do not rejoice over him, and at his tripping do not lift yourself up,
for the Lord will see, and it will not please Him, and He will turn His wrath away from him.
Do not rejoice over evildoers, and do not envy sinners;
for evil people will certainly have no offspring, and the lamp of the impious will be extinguished.
Fear God, son, and the king, and disobey neither of them;
for suddenly they will punish the impious, and who will know the punishments of both?
A son who guards a word will be outside destruction, and receiving it, he has received it.
Let no falsehood from a tongue be spoken to a king, and no falsehood will ever come from his tongue.
A king’s tongue is a sword and is not made of flesh, and whoever is handed over will be crushed;
for if his wrath is sharpened, it consumes human beings with their sinews,
and devours human bones, and burns them together like a flame, so that they are inedible to young eagles.
Fear my words, son, and receive them and repent. Thus says the man to those who trust in God, and I cease:
For I am the most foolish of all people, and human understanding is not in me.
God has taught me wisdom, and knowledge of holy ones I have known.

Who went up to heaven and came down? Who gathered winds in a fold of his garment? Who wrapped water in a cloak? Who took hold of all the ends of the earth? What is his name, or what is his children’s name, so that you may know?
All God’s words have been refined by fire, and He shields those who revere Him.
Do not add to His words, so that He may not reprove you and you become false.
Two things I ask from Thee; do not take favor away from me before I die:
Put a vain and false word far from me; give me neither wealth nor poverty; assign me what is needed and sufficient,
so that I may not become full and false and say, “Who sees me?” or become poor and steal and swear by the name of God.
Do not hand a household servant over into a master’s hands, lest he curse you and you be destroyed.
Evil offspring curse a father and do not bless the mother.
Evil offspring judge themselves righteous, but have not washed away their discharge.
Evil offspring have lofty eyes and exalt themselves with their eyelids.
Evil offspring have swords for teeth and cutting blades for molars, to consume and devour the lowly from the earth and their poor from among people.
These things I say to you, the wise, to recognize: to show deference to a face in judgment is not good;
One who says of the impious, “He is righteous,” will be accursed among peoples and hated among nations;
but those who reprove will appear better, and a good blessing will come upon them;
and lips answering good words will kiss.
Prepare your works for going out, and make yourself ready for the field, and follow behind me, and you will rebuild your house.
Do not be a false witness against your fellow citizen, and do not make your lips wide;
Do not say, “As he treated me, I will treat him, and I will punish him for the wrong he did me.”
A foolish man is like a cultivated field, and a person lacking understanding like a vineyard;
if you leave him alone, he will become wasteland, and grow wild with grass all over and become abandoned, and his stone fences are torn down.
Afterward I reconsidered; I looked so as to choose discipline.
“A little I doze, a little I sleep, a little I clasp my chest with my hands”—
but if you do this, your poverty will come marching in front, and your want like a good runner.
The leech had three daughters, dearly loved, and these three did not fill her, and the fourth was not content to say, “Enough!”
Hades and a woman’s desire, and Tartarus and land not filled with water, and water and fire will certainly not say, “It is enough.”
An eye mocking a father and dishonoring a mother’s old age—may ravens from the ravines peck it out, and may young eagles devour it.
Three things are impossible for me to understand, and the fourth I do not comprehend:
the tracks of a flying eagle, and the ways of a snake upon a rock, and the paths of a seagoing ship, and the ways of a man in youth.
Such is the way of an adulterous woman: when she has acted, she washes herself and says she has done nothing improper.
Through three things the earth is shaken, and it cannot bear the fourth:
if a household servant becomes king, and a fool is filled with food,
and if a maidservant casts out her own mistress, and if a hated woman obtains a good husband.
Four things are smallest upon the earth, yet these are wiser than the wise:
the ants, which have no strength, yet prepare their food in summer;
and the rock badgers, a nation without strength, which made their own houses in rocks;
the locust is without a king, yet marches out in good order at one command;
And the lizard, bracing itself with its hands and being easily caught, lives in a king’s fortifications.
Three things go on their way well, and the fourth moves beautifully:
a lion’s cub, stronger than beasts, which does not turn back or shrink from a beast;
and a spirited rooster walking among hens, and a male goat leading a flock, and a king addressing a nation.
If you give yourself over to merriment and stretch out your hand with fighting, you will be dishonored.
Milk out milk, and there will be butter; but if you squeeze nostrils, blood will come out; and if you drag out words, disputes and battles will come out.
My words have been spoken by God, an oracle concerning a king whom his mother instructed.
What will you keep, child? What? God’s sayings. Firstborn, I speak to you, son. What, child of my womb? What, child of my vows?
Do not give women your wealth, or your mind and livelihood to belated counsel.
Do everything with counsel; drink wine with counsel. The powerful are hot-tempered, but let them not drink wine,
so that, after drinking, they may not forget wisdom and become entirely unable to judge the weak rightly.
Give intoxicating drink to those in grief, and wine to drink to those in pain,
so that they may forget their poverty and no longer remember their troubles.
Open your mouth for God’s word, and judge everyone soundly.
Open your mouth and judge justly, and decide the case of the poor and weak.
These are Solomon’s undifferentiated instructions, which the friends of Hezekiah, king of Judea, copied out.
God’s glory conceals a word, but a king’s glory honors matters.
Heaven is high and earth deep, but a king’s heart is beyond examination.
Beat unapproved silver, and it will be cleansed, entirely pure;
Kill the impious from before a king, and his throne will prosper in righteousness.
Do not boast before a king, and do not station yourself in the places of rulers;
for it is better for you to be told, “Come up to me,” than for him to humble you before a ruler. Say what your eyes have seen.
Do not rush quickly into battle, so that you do not regret it at the end. When your friend reproaches you,
withdraw backward; do not show contempt,
lest the friend reproach you, and your battle and enmity not depart, but be for you equal to death.
Favor and friendship set one free; keep these for yourself so that you do not become subject to reproach, but guard your ways with readiness to be reconciled.
A golden apple on a carnelian necklace—so is speaking a word.
A costly carnelian is fastened into a golden earring—a wise word into a receptive ear.
As snow coming forth benefits people in harvest heat, so a faithful messenger benefits those who sent him; for he benefits the lives of those who employ him.
Like winds and clouds and very conspicuous rains, so are those who boast of a false gift.
In patience is prosperity for kings, and a soft tongue crushes bones.
Having found honey, eat what is sufficient, lest you become full and vomit.
Bring your foot rarely to your own friend, lest he become filled with you and hate you.
A club and sword and barbed arrow—so also is a man testifying false testimony against his friend.
An evil person’s tooth and a lawless person’s foot will perish on an evil day.
As vinegar is unsuitable for a wound, so a suffering that falls upon the body pains the heart.
As a moth harms a garment and a worm wood, so a man’s grief harms the heart.
If your enemy is hungry, feed him; if he is thirsty, give him drink;
for by doing this you will heap coals of fire upon his head, and the Lord will repay you good things.
A north wind raises clouds, but a shameless face provokes a tongue.
Better to dwell on a corner of a roof than with an abusive wife in a shared house.
As cold water is welcome to a thirsty life, so is good news from a faraway land.
As if someone blocked a spring and ruined an outlet of water, so it is disorderly for a righteous person to have fallen before the impious.
Eating much honey is not good, but one must honor glorious words.
As a city with its walls cast down and unwalled, so is a man who does something without counsel.
Like dew at harvest and rain in summer, so honor does not belong to a fool.
As birds and sparrows fly, so an empty curse will come upon no one.
As a whip for a horse and a goad for a donkey, so a rod for a lawless nation.
Do not answer a fool in relation to his foolishness, so that you do not become like him;
but answer a fool according to his foolishness, so that he does not appear wise to himself.
One who sends a word through a foolish messenger will drink reproach from his own feet.
Remove walking from legs, and a proverb from the mouth of fools.
One who binds a stone in a sling is like one who gives glory to a fool.
Thorns grow in the hand of the drunkard, but slavery is in the hand of fools.
All the flesh of fools is greatly storm-tossed, for their distraction is shattered.
Like a dog that comes upon its own vomit and becomes hateful is a fool who has returned in his own wickedness to his own sin.
There is shame that brings on sin, and there is shame that is glory and favor.
I saw a man who thought himself wise, yet a fool had more hope than he.
A lazy person sent on a journey says, “A lion is in the roads!”
As a door turns on its hinge, so a lazy person on his bed.
A lazy person, having hidden his hand in his lap, will not be able to bring it to his mouth.
The lazy person appears wiser to himself than one who brings back a message in full.
As one who grasps a dog’s tail, so is one who presides over another’s dispute.
As healers put forward words to people, and the first to meet the word will be tripped up,
so are all who ambush their own friends, and when detected say, “I did it in play.”
With much wood a fire flourishes, but where there is no double-minded person, battle is quiet.
A hearth for coals and wood for fire, and an abusive man for the turmoil of battle.
The words of tricksters are soft, but they strike into the store-chambers of the inward parts.
Silver given with deceit must be regarded like a potsherd; smooth lips cover a painful heart.
A weeping enemy agrees to everything with his lips, but in his heart devises deceits;
if the enemy entreats you with a loud voice, do not be persuaded, for seven evils are in his life.
One who hides enmity establishes deceit, but one well known in councils discloses his own sins.
One who digs a pit for his neighbor will fall into it, and one who rolls a stone rolls it upon himself.
A false tongue hates truth, but an unrestrained mouth makes disorders.
Do not boast of things for tomorrow, for you do not know what the coming day will bear.
Let your neighbor praise you, and not your mouth, another, and not your lips.
A stone is heavy and sand hard to carry, but a fool’s anger is heavier than both.
Wrath is merciless and anger sharp, but jealousy bears with no one.
Open rebukes are better than concealed friendship.
A friend’s wounds are more trustworthy than an enemy’s willing kisses.
A life in fullness mocks honeycombs, but to a needy life even bitter things seem sweet.
As when a bird flies down from its own nest, so a person is enslaved when estranged from his own places.
The heart delights in perfumes and wines and incense, but the life is torn apart by misfortunes.
Do not abandon your friend or an ancestral friend, and do not enter your brother’s house when misfortune strikes you; a nearby friend is better than a brother dwelling far away.
Become wise, son, so that my heart may rejoice, and turn reproachful words away from yourself.
A resourceful person hid when evils approached, but fools who went on will pay a penalty.
Take away his garment, for he has transgressed; one who ruins another’s property is insolent.
One who blesses a friend early with a loud voice will seem no different from one cursing.
Drops drive a man from his house on a wintry day, and likewise an abusive wife from his own house.
The north wind is a harsh wind, but by name it is called favorable.
Iron sharpens iron, but a man provokes the face of a companion.
One who plants a fig tree will eat its fruits, and one who guards his own master will be honored.
As faces are not like faces, so neither are human hearts.
Hades and destruction are not filled, and likewise human eyes are insatiable.
One who fixes an eye is an abomination to the Lord, and the uneducated are unrestrained in tongue.
A test for silver and gold is burning, but a man is tested through the mouth of those who praise him.
A lawless person’s heart searches out evils, but an upright heart searches out knowledge.
If you whip a fool in the midst of a council, dishonoring him, you will certainly not strip away his foolishness.
Know thoroughly the lives of your flock, and set your heart upon your herds;
for a man’s might and strength do not last for ever, nor does he hand them on from generation to generation.
Care for the green growth in the plain, and you will cut grass, and gather mountain fodder,
so that you may have sheep for clothing; value a plain, so that you may have lambs.
Son, from me you have strong sayings for your life, and for the life of your attendants.
An impious person flees when no one pursues, but a righteous person is confident like a lion.
Through the sins of the impious, disputes arise, but a prudent man will extinguish them.
A man vigorous in impieties extorts the poor. Just like a violent and useless rain,
so those who abandon the law praise impiety, but those who love the law surround themselves with a wall.
Evil men will not understand judgment, but those who seek the Lord will understand in everything.
Better a poor person walking in truth than a lying rich person.
An understanding son keeps the law, but one who tends dissipation dishonors a father.
One who increases his wealth with interest and gains gathers it for one who shows mercy to the poor.
One who turns his ear aside so as not to hear the law has himself also abhorred his own prayer.
One who leads the upright astray on an evil way will himself fall into destruction; but the lawless will pass by good things and will not enter into them.
A rich man is wise in his own estimation, but an intelligent poor person will judge him.
Through the help of the righteous much glory comes about, but in the places of the impious people are captured.
One who covers his own impiety will not prosper, but one who explains reproofs will be loved.
Happy is a man who shrinks from everything out of reverence, but one hard of heart will fall into evils.
One who tyrannizes over a needy nation while himself poor is a hungry lion and a thirsty wolf.
A king lacking revenues is a great extortioner, but one who hates injustice will live a long time.
One who acts as guarantor for a man charged with murder will be a fugitive and will not be secure.
Discipline a son, and he will love you and give adornment to your life; you must not heed a lawless nation.
One who walks righteously has been helped, but one who walks crooked ways will become entangled.
One who works his own land will be filled with bread, but one who pursues leisure will be filled with poverty.
A trustworthy man will be greatly blessed, but the evil person will not be unpunished.
One who has no respect for the faces of the righteous is not good; such a person will sell a man for a morsel of bread.
A grudging man hastens to become rich and does not know that a merciful person will rule over him.
One who reproves a person’s ways will have more favor than one who flatters with the tongue.
One who casts away a father or mother and thinks he is not sinning is a partner of an impious man.
An insatiable man judges rashly, but one who trusts in the Lord will be cared for.
One who trusts in a rash heart is a fool; but one who walks in wisdom will be saved.
One who gives to the poor will not be in need; but one who turns away his eye will be in great difficulty.
In the places of the impious the righteous groan, but at their destruction the righteous will multiply.
Better a man who reproves than a stiff-necked man; for when the latter suddenly burns, there is no healing.
When the righteous are praised, peoples will rejoice; but when the impious rule, men groan.
When a man loves wisdom, his father rejoices; but one who tends prostitutes will destroy wealth.
A righteous king raises up a country, but a lawless man tears it down.
One who prepares a net before his own friend’s face wraps it around his own feet.
For a sinning man there is a great snare, but a righteous person will be in joy and gladness.
A righteous person knows how to judge for the needy, but the impious person will not understand knowledge, and a poor person has no discerning mind.
Pestilent men set a city ablaze, but wise people turned away wrath.
A wise man judges nations, but a worthless man who becomes angry is laughed at and does not shrink back.
Men sharing in bloodshed will hate a holy person, but the upright will seek his life.
A fool brings out all his anger, but a wise person stores it up portion by portion.
When a king listens to an unjust word, all those under him are lawless.
When lender and debtor come together, the Lord inspects both.
When a king judges the poor in truth, his throne will be established as a testimony.
Blows and reproofs give wisdom, but a wandering child shames his parents.
When the impious are many, sins become many, but the righteous become terrified when those people fall.
Discipline your son, and he will give you rest and give adornment to your life.
There will certainly be no interpreter for a lawless nation, but one who keeps the law is blessed.
A harsh household servant will not be disciplined by words; for even if he understands, he will not obey.
If you see a man swift in words, know that a fool has more hope than he.
One who lives extravagantly from childhood will become a household servant, and in the end he will grieve over himself.
A wrathful man digs up strife, and an angry man dug out sins.
Insolence brings a man low, but the Lord supports the humble-minded with glory.
One who shares with a thief hates his own life; but if, when an oath is set before them, those who heard do not report,
having feared and felt shame before people, they were tripped up; but one who trusts in the Lord will rejoice. Impiety gives a man a fall; but one who trusts in the Master will be saved.
Many court the faces of leaders, but what is just for a man comes from the Lord.
An unjust man is an abomination to the righteous, but a straightening way is an abomination to a lawless person.
A courageous woman—who will find her? Such a woman is more precious than costly stones.
Her husband’s heart is confident in her; such a woman will not lack fine spoils.
For she works good things for her husband throughout her life.
Spinning wool and flax, she made useful work with her hands.
She became like a ship trading from afar, and she gathers her livelihood.
And she rises in the night and gave food to the household and tasks to the maidservants.
After inspecting a farm she bought it, and from the fruits of her hands she planted an estate.
Having girded her waist strongly, she braced her arms for work.
She tasted that working is good, and her lamp is not extinguished throughout the night.
She stretches her forearms toward profitable things, and braces her hands on a spindle.
She opened her hands to a needy person and stretched out her wrist to a poor person.
Her husband is not anxious about those at home when he stays away somewhere, for all those with her are clothed.
She made double cloaks for her husband, and garments of fine linen and purple for herself.
Her husband becomes distinguished in the gates when he sits in council with the elder inhabitants of the land.
She made linen cloths and sold them, and girdles for the Canaanites.
She opened her mouth attentively and lawfully and prescribed order for her tongue.
She clothed herself in strength and dignity and rejoiced in the last days.
The occupations of her houses are secure, and she did not eat idle food.
She opens her mouth wisely and according to law, and her mercy raised up her children, and they became wealthy, and her husband praised her:
“Many daughters acquired wealth, many did mighty things, but you stand above and have surpassed them all.”
A woman’s pleasing qualities are false and beauty is vain; for an understanding woman is blessed, and let her praise the fear of the Lord.
Give her from the fruits of her hands, and let her husband be praised in the gates.

units.text: Wisdom is celebrated at the exits, and in the squares she speaks openly.
At the tops of walls she is proclaimed; at rulers’ gates she sits nearby, and at city gates she speaks boldly:
Son, if you receive an utterance of my commandment and hide it within yourself,
your ear will obey wisdom, and you will apply your heart to understanding; you will also apply it to admonishing your son.
for if you call upon wisdom and give your voice to understanding, and seek perception with a loud voice,
and if you seek it like silver and search it out like treasures,
then you will understand the fear of the Lord and find the knowledge of God.
For the Lord gives wisdom, and from His presence come knowledge and understanding.
He stores up salvation for those acting rightly; He will shield their journey,
to guard the ways of righteous ordinances, and He will protect the way of those who revere Him.
Then you will understand righteousness and judgment, and you will make all good courses straight.
Trust God with your whole heart; do not exalt yourself in your own wisdom.
In all your ways acknowledge her, that she may cut your ways straight; and your foot will surely not stumble.
Do not be prudent in your own estimation; fear God and turn away from every evil.
Son, attend to my utterance; apply your ear to my words,
so that your springs do not fail you; keep them in your heart,
for there is life for those who find them and healing for all flesh.
Son, attend to my wisdom, and incline your ear to my words,
so that you may guard good understanding. I command you to heed the discernment of my lips.
Do not attend to a base woman, for honey drips from a prostitute’s lips; for a time she oils your throat.
Afterward, however, you will find it more bitter than gall and sharper than a two-edged blade.
For folly’s feet lead those who engage with her down with death into Hades; her tracks are not firmly set.
For she does not travel life’s ways; her tracks are slippery and not easy to recognize.
Now therefore, son, listen to me, and do not make my words ineffective.
Put your way far from her; do not approach the doors of her houses,
so that you do not surrender your life to others and your livelihood to the merciless,
so that outsiders are not filled with your strength, and your labors enter outsiders’ houses,
and you will come to regret it at the end, when the flesh of your body is worn away,
and you will say, “How I hated discipline! My heart turned aside from rebukes.
I did not listen to the voice of the one disciplining and teaching me, nor incline my ear.
I was nearly in every kind of evil in the midst of the assembly and congregation.”
Drink waters from your vessels and from your spring wells.
Do not let waters overflow for you from your spring; but let your waters travel into your own squares.
Let them belong to you alone, and let no outsider share with you.
Let your fountain of water be your own, and share joy with the wife of your youth.

Let a deer of affection and a colt of your graces keep company with you. Let your own woman lead you and be with you at every time, for as you move in the company of her affection, you will be one among many.
Do not be much involved with another woman, nor be held in the arms of one who is not your own.
For a man’s ways are before God’s eyes, and He watches all his tracks.
Lawless acts hunt a man, and each is bound tight by the cords of his own sins.
He dies among the undisciplined; from the abundance of his own life he was cast out and perished through folly.
Go to the ant, sluggard; see its ways and emulate them, and become wiser than it.
For although it has no cultivated field, and has no one forcing it, and is under no master,
it prepares its food in summer and makes abundant provision at harvest.
Or go to the bee and learn how industrious she is, and how nobly she performs her work,
whose labors kings and private people use for health; she is desired by everyone and held in esteem.
Although weak in bodily strength, she was advanced because she honored wisdom.
How long will you remain lying down, sluggard? When will you rise from sleep?
You sleep a little, sit a little, doze a little, and clasp your chest with your hands a little;
then poverty arrives beside you like an evil traveler, and want like a good runner.
But if you are diligent, your harvest will come like a spring, and want will desert you like a bad runner.
A foolish and lawless man travels ways that are not good;
the same man signals with his eye and gives signs with his foot, and instructs by gestures of his fingers;
with a twisted heart he devises evils at every time. Such a person stirs up disturbances for a city.
Therefore his destruction comes suddenly: a cutting down and an incurable crushing,
because he rejoices in everything the Lord hates, and is crushed because of his soul’s uncleanness:
But the adulterer, through lack of sense, brings destruction upon his own life;
he bears pains and dishonors, and his reproach will never be wiped away.
For her husband’s anger is full of jealousy; he will not spare on the day of judgment,
he will not trade his enmity for any ransom, nor be reconciled by many gifts.
I, Wisdom, have made counsel my dwelling, and I have called upon knowledge and reflection.
The fear of the Lord hates injustice, insolence and arrogance and the ways of wicked people; and I hate the perverted ways of evil people.
Counsel and security are mine; understanding is mine, and strength is mine.
Through me kings reign, and rulers write righteousness.
Through me great men become great, and through me sovereigns rule the earth.
I love those who love me, and those who seek me will find me.
Wealth and glory belong to me, and possession of many things and righteousness.
It is better to reap me than gold and precious stone, and my produce is better than choice silver.
I walk in ways of righteousness, and move in the midst of paths of just judgment,
so that I may apportion substance to those who love me, and fill their storehouses with good things.
Wisdom built herself a house, and set seven pillars beneath it.
She slaughtered her own sacrificial animals, mixed her own wine in a mixing-bowl, and prepared her own table.
She sent her own servants, summoning with a lofty proclamation to the mixing-bowl, saying:
“Whoever is foolish, let him turn aside to me!” And to those lacking understanding she said:
“Come, eat of my loaves, and drink wine that I mixed for you.
Leave foolishness, and you will live; seek understanding, so that you may live, and set insight right in knowledge.”
One who disciplines evil people will receive dishonor for himself, and one who reproves an impious person will bring blame on himself.
Do not reprove evil people, so that they may not hate you; reprove a wise person, and he will love you.
Give a wise person a starting point, and he will be wiser; inform a righteous person, and he will receive still more.
The beginning of wisdom is the fear of the Lord, and the counsel of holy ones is understanding.
For knowing the law belongs to a good mind.
For in this way you will live a long time, and years of your life will be added to you.
Son, if you become wise for yourself, you will also be wise for your neighbors; but if you turn out evil, you alone will bear evils.
Righteousness cuts blameless paths straight, but impiety falls into injustice.
The righteousness of upright men rescues them, but lawless people are caught in their own destruction.
When a righteous man dies, hope does not perish, but the boast of the impious perishes.
The righteous escapes from the hunt, but the impious is handed over in his place.
In the mouth of the impious is a trap for citizens, but the discernment of the righteous has a good course.
Through the good things of the righteous a city prospered,
but by the mouths of the impious it was razed.
One lacking understanding sneers at citizens, but an intelligent man keeps quiet.
A double-tongued man reveals plans in a council, but one faithful in breath conceals matters.
Those who have no steering fall like leaves, but deliverance is in much counsel.
A quick-tempered man prepares battles, but a patient person calms even a battle about to begin.
A patient man will extinguish disputes, but the impious stirs them up still more.
The ways of the idle are strewn with thorns, but those of the courageous are well worn.
As silver and gold are tested in a furnace, so hearts are chosen before the Lord.
An evil person heeds the tongue of lawless people, but a righteous person pays no attention to lying lips.
One who laughs at the poor provokes the One who made him, and one who rejoices over someone perishing will not be acquitted; but one who has compassion will receive mercy.
Son, if your heart becomes wise, you will gladden my heart too,
and your lips will spend time in words with my lips, if the words are upright.
Do not let your heart envy sinners, but be in the fear of the Lord the whole day;
for if you keep these things, you will have offspring, and your hope will not depart.
Repay no one evil for evil. Take thought for what is honorable before all people.
If possible, as far as it depends on you, live at peace with all people.
Do not avenge yourselves, beloved, but make room for wrath; for it is written, “Vengeance is Mine; I will repay, says the Lord.”
But if your enemy is hungry, feed him; if he is thirsty, give him a drink; for by doing this you will heap coals of fire upon his head.
Do not be conquered by evil, but conquer evil with good.
Submit yourselves to every human institution for the Lord’s sake, whether to a king as supreme,
or to governors as sent by him for the punishment of evildoers and the praise of those who do good.
For this is the will of God: that by doing good you should silence the ignorance of foolish people.
Live as free people, yet without using freedom as a covering for evil, but as slaves of God.
Honor everyone. Love the brotherhood. Fear God. Honor the king.
He told a parable to those who had been invited, noticing how they chose the foremost places at table. He said to them,
“When someone invites you to a wedding feast, do not recline in the foremost place. Someone more honored than you may have been invited by him,
and the one who invited you both will come and say to you, ‘Give this man your place.’ Then you will begin, with shame, to occupy the last place.

But when you are invited, go and recline in the last place, so that when the one who invited you comes, he will say to you, ‘Friend, move up higher.’ Then you will have honor before all who recline at table with you.
For everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, and the one who humbles himself will be exalted.”
If I told you earthly things and you do not believe, how will you believe if I tell you heavenly things?
And no one has ascended into heaven except the One who descended from heaven, the Son of Man.

And now, O Israel, hear the ordinances and the judgments which I teach you this day to do, that you may live and be multiplied, and enter and inherit the land which the Lord, the God of your fathers, gives you.
You shall not add unto the word which I command you, neither shall you take away from it; you shall keep the commandments of the Lord your God, which I command you this day.
But godliness with contentment is great gain.
For we brought nothing into the world, because neither can we carry anything out.
But having food and coverings, with these we will be content.
But those who want to become rich fall into temptation and a snare and many foolish and harmful desires, which plunge people into ruin and destruction.
For the love of money is a root of all evils, and some, reaching for it, wandered from the faith and pierced themselves with many pains.
Take heed unto yourself, lest you forget the Lord your God, and fail to keep His commandments, and His judgments, and His ordinances which I command you this day;
lest, when you have eaten and are filled, and have built good houses and dwelt in them,
and your herds and your flocks are multiplied, and your silver and your gold are multiplied, and all that you have is multiplied,
you become lifted up in heart, and forget the Lord your God, who brought you forth out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage;
Honour your father and your mother, that it may be well with you, and that your days may be long upon the good land which the Lord your God gives you.
You shall not commit adultery.
You shall not steal.
You shall not murder.
You shall not bear false witness against your neighbour.
You shall do no injustice in judgment; you shall not favour the person of the poor, neither shall you admire the person of the mighty; you shall judge your neighbour in righteousness.
You shall not go about deceitfully among your nation; you shall not conspire against the blood of your neighbour; I am the Lord your God.
You shall not hate your brother in your mind; you shall surely reprove your neighbour, and you shall not bear sin because of him.
And your hand shall not take vengeance, neither shall you remain angry with the sons of your people; and you shall love your neighbour as yourself; I am the Lord.
If therefore you offer your gift upon the altar, and there remember that your brother has something against you,
leave your gift there before the altar, and go; first be reconciled to your brother, and then come and offer your gift.
Come to terms with your adversary quickly, while you are with him on the way, lest your adversary hand you over to the judge, and the judge to the officer, and you be thrown into prison.

For if, after escaping the world’s defilements through the knowledge of the Lord and Savior Jesus Christ, they are again entangled in them and overcome, their last state has become worse than their first.
For it would have been better for them not to have known the way of righteousness than, after knowing it, to turn back from the holy commandment handed down to them.
What the true proverb says has happened to them: “A dog has returned to its own vomit,” and, “A sow, after washing, returns to wallowing in mud.”
Watch for the right time and guard against evil, and do not be ashamed concerning your soul.
For there is shame that brings sin, and there is shame that is glory and favor.
Do not show partiality against your own soul, and do not defer to someone to your own downfall.
This too I saw as wisdom under the sun, and it seemed great to me:
There was a small city with few people in it; a great king might come against it, surround it and build great siegeworks against it,
and he might find in it a poor wise man, who will deliver the city by his wisdom; yet no one remembered that poor man.
I said, Wisdom is better than strength; yet the poor man’s wisdom is despised, and his words are not heard.
The words of the wise, heard quietly, are better than the shouting of rulers in follies.
Wisdom is better than weapons of war, but one sinner will destroy much good.
The heart is deep beyond all things, and so is a human; and who will know him?
I, the Lord, examine hearts and test kidneys, to give each according to his ways and the fruits of his practices.
Happy is the husband of a good wife, and the number of his days is doubled.
A courageous wife gladdens her husband, and he will complete his years in peace.
A good wife is a good portion; she will be given among the portion of those who fear the Lord.
A wife’s grace will delight her husband, and her knowledge will fatten his bones.
A silent wife is a gift of the Lord, and there is no exchange for a disciplined soul.
A modest wife is grace upon grace, and no weight is worth a self-controlled soul.
The sun rising in the Lord’s heights—so is a good wife’s beauty in the order of her house.
A lamp shining upon a holy lampstand—so is a beautiful face upon a firmly established stature.
Golden pillars upon a silver base—so are beautiful feet upon the breast of one who stands firm.
In Joppa there was a woman disciple named Tabitha, which translated is Dorcas. She was full of good works and acts of charity.
In those days she became ill and died. They washed her and laid her in an upper room.
Since Lydda was near Joppa, the disciples, hearing that Peter was there, sent two men to him, urging, “Do not delay in coming to us.”

Peter rose and went with them. When he arrived, they brought him into the upper room. All the widows stood beside him weeping and showing the tunics and garments Dorcas had made while she was with them.
But if someone does not provide for his own, and especially his household, he has denied the faith and is worse than an unbeliever.
Let a widow be enrolled who is not less than sixty years old, a wife of one husband,
attested for good works: if she brought up children, if she received strangers, if she washed saints’ feet, if she assisted the afflicted, if she followed every good work.
Whenever you stretch your hands toward Me, I will turn My eyes away from you. Even if you multiply supplication, I will not listen to you, for your hands are full of blood.
Wash yourselves, become clean. Remove the evils from your souls, before My eyes. Stop your evil deeds.
Learn to do good, seek judgment, rescue the wronged. Give judgment for the orphan and vindicate the widow.
Woe to your strong ones who drink wine and the powerful who mix strong drink,
who justify the ungodly for gifts and take away the righteous person’s right!
But I will look toward the Lord; I will wait upon God my Savior. My God will listen to me.
Do not rejoice over me, my enemy, because I have fallen! I will rise, for if I sit in darkness, the Lord will shine for me.
I will bear the Lord’s anger, for I sinned against Him, until He vindicates my case. He will execute my judgment and bring me out into the light; I will see His righteousness.
He will say: “Hear these things now, authorities of Jacob’s house and remaining ones of Israel’s house! Is it not for you to know justice,
you who hate good things and seek evil things, who snatch their skins from them and their flesh from their bones?”
Just as they ate the flesh of My people, flayed their skins from their bones, crushed their bones and divided them into pieces like flesh for a cauldron and meat for a cooking pot,
And God put a word in Balaam's mouth and said: Return to Balak and thus you shall speak.
And he returned to him, and there he stood beside his whole burnt offerings, with all the officials of Moab.

And God's Spirit came upon him, and he took up his parable and said: Balak summoned me from Mesopotamia, the king of Moab from the eastern mountains: Come, curse Jacob for me; come, call down a curse on Israel for me.
Why should I curse whom the Lord does not curse? Why should I call down a curse on whom God does not curse?
From the tops of mountains I shall see them, and from the hills I shall observe them. Behold, a people who will dwell alone, not counted among the nations.
Who has measured Jacob’s seed exactly, and who will count Israel's clans? May my soul die among righteous souls, and may my seed be like their seed!
And Balak said to Balaam: What have you done to me? I summoned you to curse my enemies, and look, you have pronounced a blessing!
And Balaam said to Balak: Must I not take care to speak what God puts in my mouth?
Thus says the Lord: “For three impieties of Israel, and for four, I will not turn away from him, because they sold a righteous person for silver and a poor person for sandals,

which tread upon the earth’s dust. They struck the heads of the poor with their fists and turned aside the way of the humble; a son and his father went in to the same young slave woman, to profane the name of their God,
and, tying their garments with cords, they made hangings next to the altar, and drank wine from extortions in their God’s house.
The Lord’s word came to me, saying,
“Son of man, say to her, ‘You are a land not wetted, nor did rain come upon you on the day of wrath.
Her leaders within her are like roaring lions seizing prey, devouring lives with power, taking payments unjustly, and your widows have multiplied within you.

Her priests set aside My law and profaned My holy things. They did not distinguish between holy and profane, nor distinguish between unclean and clean. They covered their eyes from My Sabbaths, and I was profaned among them.
Her rulers within her are like wolves seizing prey to shed blood, so that in greed they may gain more.
Her prophets, coating them, will fall, seeing vain things, divining falsehoods, saying, “Thus says the Lord,” when the Lord has not spoken,
oppressing the people of the land unjustly and seizing plunder, oppressing the poor and needy and not dealing justly with the sojourner.
What the caterpillar left, the locust devoured; what the locust left, the bruchus locust devoured; what the bruchus locust left, the blight devoured.
Blow a trumpet in Zion! Proclaim on My holy mountain, and let all who inhabit the land be thrown into turmoil, because the Lord’s day is present; it is near,

a day of darkness and gloom, a day of cloud and mist. Like dawn a numerous and strong people will be poured over the mountains. Its like has never existed, nor will another follow it through the years, for generations upon generations.
Before it is consuming fire, and behind it a kindled flame. The land before its face is like a garden of delight, and behind it a desolate plain; no one will escape it.
Their appearance is like the sight of horses; like riders they will pursue.
With a sound like chariots they will leap upon mountain peaks, like the sound of a fiery flame devouring stubble, like a numerous and strong people arrayed for war.
Before it peoples will be crushed; every face is like the scorching of a pot.
Like fighters they will run, and like soldiers they will climb the walls. Each will go on his own road, and they certainly will not turn aside from their paths,
and no one will hold back from his brother. Burdened with their weapons they will go, and among their missiles they will fall, yet they will certainly not be destroyed.
They will seize the city and run upon the walls; they will climb upon the houses and enter through windows like thieves.
Before them the earth will be thrown into turmoil and heaven shaken; the sun and moon will grow dark, and the stars will sink their brightness.

The Lord will give His voice before His force, because His camp is very large, because the works of His words are strong. For the Lord’s day is great, great and very manifest; who will be sufficient for it?
But let the one who boasts boast in the Lord.
For it is not the one who commends himself who is approved, but the one whom the Lord commends.
While He was still speaking, behold, Judas, one of the twelve, came with a great crowd carrying swords and clubs, from the chief priests and elders of the people.
The one handing Him over had given them a sign, saying, “The One I kiss is He; seize Him.”
Immediately he came to Jesus and said, “Greetings, Rabbi,” and kissed Him.
Jesus said to him, “Friend, do what you have come for.” Then they came forward, laid their hands upon Jesus, and seized Him.
And the Lord said, “Who, then, is the faithful steward, the prudent one, whom his master will appoint over his household staff to give out their ration of grain at the proper time?
Blessed is that slave whom his master finds doing so when he comes.
Truly, I tell you, he will appoint him over all his possessions.
Likewise, wives, submit yourselves to your own husbands, so that even if some disobey the word, they may be won without a word through the conduct of their wives,
when they observe your pure conduct in fear.
Let your adornment not be the outward kind—braiding hair, putting on gold ornaments, or dressing in garments—
but the hidden person of the heart, in the imperishable beauty of a gentle and quiet spirit, which is very precious before God.
For this is how the holy women of former times, who hoped in God, also adorned themselves, submitting themselves to their own husbands,
as Sarah obeyed Abraham, calling him lord. You have become her children if you do good and do not fear any terror.
